requirements.requirement_text: AWS KMS operations run behind a narrowly scoped AWS API Gateway endpoint and a small credential-kms-bridge Lambda. The Lambda's AWS execution role can invoke only GenerateDataKey, Decrypt and ReEncrypt on the named environment KEK ARN; it has no access to Vault D1 or provider BYOK. The Vault Worker calls the bridge with a short-lived, audience-bound signed request using a per-Worker Tier A signing secret. The bridge validates Worker identity, environment, request nonce, tenant/app/credential context and allowed operation before calling KMS. No long-lived AWS access key is placed in a Worker, source file, queue or D1. The bridge returns a plaintext DEK only over authenticated TLS for immediate in-memory use, plus the wrapped DEK. Worker logs and traces omit both values. This cross-cloud path is a proposed design and must be provisioned/tested before use; until then, Tier C writes and reads fail closed.

requirements.requirement_text: Chat, browser UI, desktop WebView, HTTPS and MCP are separate clients of one server-side typed action registry. Each action defines schema/version, required principal and capability, audience, data class, effect class, budget semantics, idempotency behavior, confirmation threshold and audit fields. The UI cannot add an action by rendering model-generated HTML/JS. The headless API cannot bypass checks that are applied in Chat.

requirements.requirement_text: The device initiates outbound WSS using TLS 1.3, validates the server certificate chain and expected hostname, and has no insecure downgrade or certificate-validation bypass. The Runner exposes no public incoming TCP/HTTP/WebSocket/SSH/RDP listener and no permanent device-IP allowlist is required. Bounded HTTPS polling is an availability fallback using the same device proof, nonce, short-lived session, lease, signature and revoke checks; it is not weaker authentication. Cloudflare Tunnel may provide a targeted outbound private-network route for a specific workload, but it is not device identity or per-job authorization. Service Tokens are not a fleet lifetime identity. Optional Access mTLS is defense in depth and must be verified for the actual hostname, account plan and ingress path; Workers outbound mTLS binding is not a substitute for Runner ingress authentication. Worker-level Access policy may reject WSS upgrade with 403, so a selected Access layer uses hostname-based policy and still requires application proof.
